USE syllable machine: Ragel-table interpreter that tags each glyph with its syllable (serial << 4 | kind).

Ports harfrust ot/shaper/use_machine.rs. The transition lookup follows the flat char_class / indices / index_defaults backend of that file; the driver loop, look-ahead memo and cond-action dispatch mirror khmer_machine.nim.

../buffer, use_machine_data

Types

SyllableType = enum
  IndependentCluster = 0,   ## Independent cluster.
  ViramaTerminatedCluster,  ## Virama terminated cluster.
  SakotTerminatedCluster,   ## Sakot terminated cluster.
  StandardCluster,          ## Standard cluster.
  NumberJoinerTerminatedCluster, ## Number joiner terminated cluster.
  NumeralCluster,           ## Numeral cluster.
  SymbolCluster,            ## Symbol cluster.
  HieroglyphCluster,        ## Hieroglyph cluster.
  BrokenCluster,            ## Broken cluster.
  NonCluster                 ## Non cluster.
USE syllable shape. Note IndependentCluster comes first, matching harfrust; only the actions below emit the rest. 
UseSyllableLookaheadMemo = object
  seen*: seq[(uint32, uint32)]
Remembers (position, machine state) pairs an earlier token already scanned through without matching, so a later token that reaches the same pair can fall back to te right away. The state is high(uint32) while unseen. Allocated lazily on the first look-ahead past UseMaxSyllableLookahead.

proc findSyllablesUse(buf: var Buffer) {....raises: [], tags: [], forbids: [].}
Runs the syllable machine over the buffer, tagging syllables and setting the broken-syllable scratch flag. Mirrors harfrust find_syllables, including the EOF transition pass. 
proc isDoomedRevisit(memo: var UseSyllableLookaheadMemo; p, ts, cs, len: int): bool {.
    ...raises: [], tags: [], forbids: [].}
Returns true when (p, cs) was already visited by an earlier token (one with a smaller start ts) and can therefore be cut short. Otherwise records this visit and returns false.

Builds an empty memo; the backing store is allocated on first use.
